draft.title: Predictive maintenance of tunnel kilns and automated production scheduling at Ceramika Wartka
draft.summary: Ceramika Wartka Sp. z o.o. plans to roll out predictive maintenance for its tunnel kilns and automated production scheduling. Dig.IT 2/2026 fits the company's profile, but two conditions — a positive net result and an available de minimis limit — must be confirmed before applying.

sections.heading: Problem and current situation
sections.body:
The company (160 people) makes ceramic tiles. Its tunnel kilns break down unpredictably, and the production schedule is planned by hand in a spreadsheet.

[To complete: number and duration of unplanned kiln stoppages and their cost over the last 12 months.]

sections.heading: Solution and project scope
sections.body:
1. Collecting the tunnel kiln data needed to predict failures.
2. An AI model that flags kiln failure risk to the maintenance team.
3. An automated production scheduling tool to replace the spreadsheet.
4. Team training — as an additional cost, within the 40% limit of eligible costs.

[To complete: scope of the sensor installation and contractors selected on the basis of at least 3 quotes.]

sections.heading: Results and indicators
sections.body:
Fewer unplanned kiln stoppages; the production schedule built automatically instead of in a spreadsheet.

[To complete with baseline and target values: number of unplanned stoppages, time needed to prepare the schedule.]

sections.heading: Budget and schedule
sections.body:
Dig.IT 2/2026: grant of PLN 150–850k, up to 50% of eligible costs, de minimis aid, reimbursed after the project ends. The grant may not exceed 30% of average annual net revenue over the last 3 years.

[To complete: budget from the quotes, own contribution, schedule of stages 1–4.]
